pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING – LETTERS OF APPLICATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing – Letters of Application

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing – Letters of Application
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why do we make applications whenever we need formal opportunities?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. recognise the components of a letter of application for information
2. write a letter of application for a scholarship for effective communication

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing – Letters of Application

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing – Letters of Application

Teach
• Focus skill: recognise the components of a letter of application for information.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing – Letters of Application.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing – Letters of Application
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we make applications whenever we need formal opportunities?
2. How do application letters differ from other letters?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
